questions.q: F(x) = x² − 4. Give the turning point of (a) y = f(x) + 3 (b) y = f(x − 1) (c) y = −f(x)
questions.model: (a) Up 3: (0, −4) becomes (0, −1). (b) Right 1: (1, −4). (c) Reflect in the x-axis: (0, 4), now a maximum.

questions.q: Describe how y = cos x maps to y = cos(x − 90°). Where is the maximum of y = cos(x − 90°) for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°?
questions.a: Translation 90° to the right (B1 B1); maximum at (90°, 1) (B1)

questions.q: Describe the single transformation that maps y = x² onto y = x² + 6x + 4.
(4, 1) is on y = f(x). Give its image on y = f(x + 2), y = −f(x), y = 3f(x) and y = f(2x).
questions.model: f(x + 2): x moves 2 left: (2, 1). −f(x): y changes sign: (4, −1). 3f(x): y × 3: (4, 3). f(2x): x halves: (2, 1).
